⭐ 0 stars – absolutely not recommended

One of the most disappointing experiences I have had with a veterinary clinic. Unfortunately, this is not the first time. This is now the third time that, after a visit, I feel that unnecessary costs are being charged.

Today, I came with my dog ​​solely for blood and urine tests. My dog ​​had actually already been to the vet last week for a consultation, for which I simply paid the bill. Yet, today, a vet consultation was added to the bill again.

The first bill was over €200. After I objected to this, the amount was adjusted to approximately €181. Eventually, I was told that I had to pay €139. But even that €139 included the vet's consultation, even though I had not scheduled a consultation today at all. After all, that consultation had already taken place last week.

Moreover, I had the email with me clearly stating that the senior screening cost €139. So, I came today purely for the scheduled tests. However, I had to explain several times myself why a new consultation should not be charged.

I also found the blood draw particularly unprofessional. Multiple attempts were required, and ultimately, not even enough blood was drawn. My dog ​​suffered an unnecessary amount of stress because of this. Subsequently, the bill was discussed again, as well as what financial adjustments needed to be made.

What disappoints me most is that in almost every discussion, it ultimately seems to be about money and the bill again. As an owner, I want my dog ​​to be looked at first: what does she need, does she feel safe, and is she being treated calmly and carefully?

In my opinion, the veterinarian/surgeon in question also barely took the time to properly assess my dog. She was finished within a few minutes. My dog ​​clearly did not feel comfortable with her from the start and even bit her. I have never seen my dog ​​react like this during a veterinary visit.

I expect professionalism, expertise, patience, clear communication, and above all, love and respect for animals from a veterinary clinic. Unfortunately, I absolutely did not experience that today. After three negative experiences, I have reached my limit. I do not want to have to check the bill after every visit to see what costs have appeared on it for no apparent reason. And I do not want to subject my dog ​​to treatment again where I feel there is insufficient attention paid to her well-being.

I have completely lost my trust in this clinic and will not be returning. Based on my experiences, I am unfortunately absolutely unable to recommend this clinic.

Hi Percy,

Thank you for your positive review. We would be happy to pass on your appreciation to our team.

Kind regards,

On August 11, I took my dog ​​Kayra to this vet because she had been coughing slightly again for a few weeks. About six months earlier, X-rays had been taken at another animal hospital. These showed that she had a murmur in her lungs, but no fluid or serious symptoms yet. She was given medication to which she responded very well: the coughing disappeared, and for a long time, she was free of any other problems.

The night before our appointment, I called the emergency vet as a precaution. I was told that I could bring Kayra in if she was severely out of breath. Because her condition was not that serious, I was advised to call her own vet the next morning. I followed that advice.

Upon arrival, the assistant and the vet reacted very panicky, and Kayra had to be placed in an oxygen chamber immediately. She was indeed panting, but she was always extremely anxious at the vet's. This was known to the practice. In the oxygen chamber, she initially calmed down again.

I told the vet that Kayra had responded very well to the medication she had received earlier from the other animal hospital. Because that medication had completely resolved her symptoms at the time, I actually asked if she could receive it again. Instead, the veterinarian suggested an injection that, according to the explanation, would allow her to breathe better.

Immediately after this injection, I saw Kayra suddenly deteriorate rapidly. I said right away that it seemed as if she was having an adverse or allergic reaction, but according to the veterinarian, an allergic reaction to this medication was not possible. After that, Kayra received another injection, and I was told that she probably would not survive that day.

Fluid and a little blood came out of her nose and mouth. I kept saying: “I didn’t bring her in like this.” According to the veterinarian, this was due to her lungs, but no new X-rays or other tests had been done at that time.

I was told that Kayra could not stay in the oxygen chamber much longer because the practice had to close earlier that day. The veterinarian said that her daughter was in the hospital and that she had to go there. I understand that, but it made the treatment feel very rushed. To me, Kayra was my child too. At such a terrible moment, I needed peace, clear explanations, care, and compassion.

It was suggested that Kayra be taken to another animal hospital by ambulance, and I was asked if I still wanted to try. Because I wanted to do everything to save her, I agreed. She received another injection to help her endure the journey, but her condition continued to deteriorate. Eventually, it was said that euthanasia was the best option. When I saw how much she was suffering, I felt that I had no other choice.

Even after Kayra had been put to sleep, my husband and I felt that we had to leave quickly. The succession of injections, her sudden decline, and the haste with which everything unfolded have left me with many questions.

I do not claim to be able to medically determine the cause of Kayra's rapid deterioration. I only know what I saw myself: I brought her in because of a slight cough, she calmed down in the oxygen chamber, and after the first injection, things suddenly went seriously wrong. That same day, I had to say goodbye to my beloved little dog.

I am left with intense grief and many unanswered questions. I especially miss a clear explanation regarding which injections Kayra received, why they were necessary, and how her condition could change so quickly. The lack of calm and empathy has made this experience even more traumatic.

At first, I could not and did not want to share this, because the grief and memories were too heavy. However, I feel that I must tell this for my own healing process. This is our personal experience, and we feel it is important to share it. Hopefully, our story will help other pet owners make an informed choice when seeking medical care for their beloved pet.

A few months ago, I had an appointment for an ultrasound of my pregnant cat. What I experienced there was downright unacceptable.

We had to wait for more than half an hour while the doctors just stood there talking. Meanwhile, my cat (who is very anxious) was visibly trembling with stress. We asked at the reception desk several times how much longer it would take, but the response was extremely unfriendly and disrespectful: “YOU MUST WAIT.” This is no way to treat paying customers.

Additionally, we got the strong feeling that we were being treated differently from other customers. People who looked “Dutch” were helped kindly, while we clearly did not seem welcome. The staff's attitude changed every time we came near. This feels not only unprofessional but also discriminatory.

The ultrasound itself lasted less than 5 minutes and was performed hastily and without interest. Moreover, inappropriate and suggestive questions were asked, as if I were using my cat to make money with kittens. Completely misplaced and insulting. This is her second litter and she is almost 3 years old.

In short: poor service, no respect for either the animal or the owner, and a very unpleasant, possibly discriminatory experience. I will absolutely not be coming back here and I do not recommend this to anyone. Foreigners are apparently not welcome here.

We received incredibly good care from this animal hospital. A sweet, calm doctor (Dominique) who took plenty of time, despite the busyness of the practice. The assistants on the phone were also kind and helpful. We came here with our dog because she had anal gland problems; her anal sacs were removed. The surgery itself was performed in Amstelveen (EDZ), which we are also very happy about. There was earlier availability there to perform the procedure, and a comprehensive anesthesia team was present. A heart ultrasound was also performed there to see if our dog could handle it well given her heart murmur. Everything went well. No more misery for our dog with her anal sacs; truly something to celebrate.

A year ago, our cat became very thin and seemed to have pain in her abdomen. Caressa had a blood test and said she had a potassium deficiency but was otherwise healthy. They couldn't explain her very thinness. We were given potassium powder. In January of this year, she didn't eat for a few days. Over the weekend, we went to the emergency clinic, where they did more blood tests and gave her an IV and something for the nausea. On Monday, we went back to Caressa because she still wasn't eating. Another IV and another test. Just like the emergency clinic, they felt that one kidney was very small and recommended an ultrasound. That was supposed to be on Tuesday. Monday evening, we received a call that the ultrasound technician was sick and we had to go to their clinic in Amstelveen. They told us that instead of the approximate price of €160, the ultrasound would cost a few hundred euros more. The same company, Evidensia. The cat ate a little that evening, so we started looking for another ultrasound location. Fortunately, the Joyce Hofman clinic was willing to do the ultrasound, but they needed our cat's records. I called Joyce Hofman several times on Wednesday, and they always promised to send the records, but they didn't, so the ultrasound couldn't go ahead. During the night from Wednesday to Thursday, the cat was so ill that she started to collapse. Thursday morning, I called Caressa again and asked what I could do because I thought my cat was dying.
The assistant tried to get a doctor on the phone, but that wasn't possible. I could come by at the end of the day. My cat had barely eaten anything for a week, and another long day of doing nothing didn't seem like an option. An earlier appointment wasn't possible; they were busy. I called Joyce Hofman, and they immediately put me in a doctor who said, "This really doesn't sound good, you need to come in right away." They did another blood test, including the thyroid, as they said this is always necessary for older cats that have lost weight. The thyroid was overactive, so a regular blood test no longer shows that the kidneys are severely impaired. Our cat's kidneys were completely destroyed, which could have been prevented if she had been properly examined a year ago and given thyroid medication. We had to put her down. We transferred our other cat and dog to Joyce Hofman, where they are more skilled, kinder, and also much cheaper. I asked Caressa to send my animals' records to Hofman, but this wasn't done either. They sent a consultation for both of them. I would advise anyone against going to an Evidensia clinic.
The staff is very nice and helpful.

Sandra Spillekoms approach to handling Feline Infectious Peritonitis (FIP) is deeply concerning and calls into question her competence and ethics as a veterinarian. She euthanized a cat diagnosed with suspected FIP and actively discouraged the owner from pursuing treatment. What's more alarming is that she allegedly refused to conduct necessary tests and falsely claimed that cats with FIP dont survive.

This kind of misinformation is not only outdated but dangerous. There are now treatments available that have shown promising results in cats with FIP, offering hope where there once was none. Denying a pet owner the option to explore these treatments, and instead opting for euthanasia without proper diagnostics, is a gross neglect of duty.

Pet owners trust veterinarians to provide the best possible care and accurate information about all available options. Her lack of empathy and up-to-date knowledge not only robbed this cat of a fighting chance but also inflicted unnecessary emotional pain on the rescuers.
Very caring, friendly and informative

A few months ago, in April 2025, I had my sick cat put to sleep. I wanted to bury my 18-year-old cat (raised since she was a kitten) so I could visit her often and remember her. After the second (lethal) injection, I asked the "veterinarian" who administered the injections if there was a pet cemetery somewhere in the Netherlands. In my emotion and the crying fits I was having at that moment, I didn't think to consult Google. The veterinarian indicated that my cat could NOT be buried ANYWHERE in the Netherlands. Next, I asked if my cat could stay in the cold storage overnight so we could look into it further. That was "possible." I thought, how kind. After my best friend breathed her last, I walked to the cashier, and to my surprise, I had to shell out 200 euros without being informed in advance. After researching at other veterinary clinics, the costs of having a cat put to sleep are between 60-90 euros, and having it put to sleep at home is between 100-150 euros. Even though I was inside for perhaps a total of 20 minutes, including the injections. The euthanasia was completed in a maximum of 10 minutes, and I was able to say a very brief goodbye since I hadn't expected my cat to be put to sleep; according to the vet, that was the best thing I could do. At that moment, you don't think about the costs and you just pay. Afterwards, I was shocked by it, and I find it very sloppy that it was so expensive. And after gathering some information, I was able to pick up my cat the next day and have it buried at a pet cemetery in Hoorn (Begraafplaats de Stille Weide, super good service). Thanks again for the good information and “service,” Caressa.
It might be nice in the future if you inform people IN ADVANCE about the costs and provide the correct information regarding burial. Oh, and I didn't get to take the towel my cat lay on to be put to sleep with me either, even though I paid 200 euros. Not recommended if you treat people this way, let alone animals. Looking back, I think, given the incorrect information I received, it was actually necessary to have my cat put to sleep, since there were no pet cemeteries in the Netherlands either. You start to doubt, and that is what I find the worst part.. No man, definitely NOT recommended after this experience, even though I used to go there all the time. Thanks for that.
PS: I hesitated for a long time to post this review, but my soul cannot help but refrain from doing so, to spare other animal lovers from this and to ask questions before you start something.

I brought my puppy in for vaccines two days ago, and this morning she woke up with a swollen face—a clear emergency. Naturally, I expected to bring her in immediately, but when I called, I was told there were no available spots. How is that possible for an emergency? You should make a spot available - I am a client how can I trust a place like this?

When I called another nearby vet, they also had no appointments but still asked me to bring her in immediately so she could be seen right away. That’s the kind of service I expected from you.

I'm extremely disappointed with how this situation was handled. In an emergency, the response should be different. This experience has really shaken my trust in your service.
I have been coming to this vet for a very long time. I see many low reviews, that is possible, but I have never been dissatisfied here; I am always helped quickly and kindly.

It’s been 5 months since the incident at Caressa that stopped me from coming here for check-ups and emergencies for my dog Oliver. I want to share what happened with us. Oliver has been a patient at Caressa for 2 years. He successfully had has puppy teeth extracted there. We were happy with the treatment and service until one Saturday we went to Caressa for an emergency regurgitation since Oliver swallowed something he shouldn’t have. A few weeks prior we had his annual check-up and the vet said everything was fine. During the emergency visit, the vet gave him the shot that would make him regurgitate and I helped my dog let it out. I was already concerned about him, as any dog parent would be. Then the vet checked his heart and told me abruptly “Your dog has a heart murmur. I’m surprised my colleague didn’t hear it.” I was shocked and asked for more information. “Are you sure? What does this mean?” She was annoyed and checked again and said “Yes I’m sure. You’ll have to come back in 4 weeks to do more testing”. I didn’t know anything about a heart murmur at that time, and to have this information dropped like a bomb to me about my 2 year old dog who just had an emergency felt cold and insensitive. When she wouldn’t give me further information to reassure me also made me feel confused and scared. What she said might seem like normal, direct behavior to others, but in my opinion, when you are in the business of animal care it’s important to be empathetic to the animals and their owners.

I proceeded to do extensive research about heart murmurs. The vet didn’t factor in that Oliver was very nervous at the appointment and that may have caused his heart to race faster. I got an appointment at another Vet, Osdorp Dierenkliniek, where Oliver went for his first puppy vaccinations, to get a second consultation. The vet assistants there were so much more sensitive and empathetic. Two of them took turns listening to his heart. And they scheduled an appointment for me with their most experienced vet to do the echohart (ultrasound). The vet said Oliver was calm and it was very quick. She said he has a Grade 1 slight murmur but his heart is very strong and sporty. The thickness of his heart is normal and there is just a slight turbulence in the flow. His behavior is what matters the most and as long as he’s sleeping, eating, and playing normally then there’s nothing to be worried about. I can count his breaths once a month and he can get a check-up every 6 months. This is the kind of treatment I expected. Therefore, I decided to no longer choose Caressa due to that disturbing incident.

It's a clinic with lots of veterinarians that change a lot. Some of them are good, some of them will put the wrong diagnosis, some of them will try to take fluid out of your cat's lung with a needle and accidentally puncture their heart. …

We received friendly service from the staff at this veterinary clinic. However, we were unnecessarily overcharged, and the internal communication was poor. On the vet's advice, we had agreed to three tests (X-rays, blood tests, and …

They are pricing themselves completely out of the market. A consultation of 67 euros without a proper examination. And then you pay extra for that. Medication (which is debatable as to whether it is truly necessary) is sold over the counter …

Great vet, Their prices are very fair and they treat your animal well. My dog got neutered at caressa and it went so smoothly. We also go here for check ups and vaccines and the staff here is just lovely.

Excellent care, responsive, good communication, but above all, incredibly sweet! Thank you so much for the fantastic care of Daantje. So glad that, thanks to you, she's recovered well and hopefully will continue to do so for a long time to come.
